title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards
abstract: arXiv:2611.13922v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Acoustic side-channel attacks (ASCA) recover typed text from the sound of keystrokes, using only a commodity microphone and no access to the victim's device. Prior work establishes that such attacks succeed under idealized laboratory conditions - a single keyboard, a fixed microphone, a quiet room, and training and testing on the same device but leaves open the question that matters for security: whether keystroke inference survives the open world of unseen keyboards, diverse users, noisy environments, and compressed transmission channels. The answer developed here is that it does, provided the acoustic model is made explicitly domain-invariant and its noisy predictions are corrected by a language model.

translated_title: 域不变与语言模型辅助的键盘声学侧信道攻击
translated_abstract: 声学侧信道攻击（ASCA）仅通过一个普通麦克风、无需访问受害者设备，即可从键盘敲击声中恢复所输入的文本。先前的研究表明，此类攻击在理想化的实验室条件下可以成功——即单一键盘、固定麦克风、安静房间，且训练和测试在同一设备上进行——但遗留了一个对安全至关重要的开放性问题：键盘敲击推断能否在更开放的真实环境中依然有效，包括未见过的键盘、不同的用户、嘈杂的环境以及经过压缩的传输信道。本文给出的答案是肯定的，前提是使声学模型具备显式的域不变性，并利用语言模型对其含噪的预测结果进行校正。
tldr: 本文证明，通过让声学模型具备显式域不变性并用语言模型校正含噪预测，声学侧信道攻击在未见过的键盘、多样用户、嘈杂环境和压缩信道等真实开放条件下仍能有效恢复键盘输入内容。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that acoustic side-channel keystroke attacks remain effective in open-world conditions of unseen keyboards, diverse users, noisy environments, and compressed channels, by making the acoustic model explicitly domain-invariant and correcting its noisy predictions with a language model.
